one_liner: Pure-Rust, Apache-2.0 FFmpeg rebuild whose MP3 decoder and frame-parallel AAC/Vorbis encoders beat FFmpeg's CLI on wall clock.
what_it_does: A Cargo workspace that reimplements FFmpeg's demux/decode/encode/mux pipeline in Rust, with an `rff`/`rffprobe` CLI that accepts common ffmpeg flags and can install under the ffmpeg/ffprobe names. The catalogued numbers belong to three standalone, zero-dependency codec crates: rusty_mp3 (MPEG-1/2/2.5 Layer III decoder and encoder), rusty_aac (AAC-LC decoder and encoder) and rusty_vorbis (encoder only). Their APIs are push/pull objects modelled on FFmpeg's EAGAIN/EOF drain protocol (`push`/`push_pcm_f32`, `next_frame`/`next_packet`, `flush`/`finish`), not libavcodec-compatible C APIs.
how_it_is_fast: MP3 decode: five bit-identical changes (an 8-byte word-load bit reader for Huffman peeks, a circularly addressed synthesis V-FIFO instead of a 960-float memmove per pass, a half-work IMDCT that derives mirrored outputs from exact symmetries of the stored cosine tables, runtime-detected AVX matrixing and windowing kept bit-exact by using separate mul+add, and a division-free Huffman pair decode), plus `decode_pipelined`, which splits entropy decoding (bit reservoir) from the transform (IMDCT overlap, synthesis FIFO) across two threads joined by a bounded channel. AAC and Vorbis encode: frame parallelism. Window decisions are made up front, then contiguous frame ranges are encoded on `available_parallelism()` scoped threads. This works because the AAC encoder has no bit reservoir (fixed per-frame budget) and the Vorbis encoder codes independent 2048-sample long blocks. N/4-point FFT MDCTs, AVX2 quantize kernels and a Vorbis energy-bucket residue-class shortlist cut per-frame cost.
when_to_use: You need MP3 decoding in a Rust or wasm program under a permissive licence with no C or FFI; the authors gate it bit-exact against FFmpeg, and it is bit-exact on wasm32-wasip1 and wasm32-unknown-unknown with zero host imports.

Offline batch transcoding of whole files to AAC-LC or Vorbis on a many-core box, where wall-clock time matters more than CPU time and the whole input can sit in memory (AAC 3.2-7.9x and Vorbis about 5.2x faster than single-threaded FFmpeg/libvorbis, first-party).
Embedding an AAC-LC or MP3 encoder in a Rust binary without FFmpeg's LGPL/GPL or FDK's licence; rusty_aac's PEAQ table has it ahead of FFmpeg's native AAC on real mono music at 128 kb/s and above.
Decoding long MP3 files already in memory on a 2-core budget: `decode_pipelined` measured 1,017 ms against FFmpeg's 1,455 ms on two physical cores.
when_not_to_use: Live or low-latency encoding: the AAC and Vorbis encoders buffer the whole stream and return `Again` from `next_packet` until `finish()`, so the parallel speedup exists only in whole-file mode.

CPU-bound single-threaded encoding or best quality per bit: single-thread Vorbis is about 1.45x slower than libvorbis and 0.6-0.7 PEAQ ODG behind on tonal music; rusty_aac has no bit reservoir or VBR and trails FFmpeg at 96 kb/s and below, on piano stereo and on noise-like content.

AAC decoding at scale, HE-AAC or more than 6 channels: the decoder's IMDCT is a naive O(N^2) f64 cosine sum (open issue #16 measured 24.4 ms per 21.3 ms frame on an EPYC 7763), SBR is not reconstructed, and 7+ channels are rejected.
Video work: VP9 decode runs at 0.16-0.21x of FFmpeg and H.264 decode about 2x behind.
Anything needing an audited, settled codebase: pre-1.0, 'not yet independently audited', 6 stars, and open issue #14 reports `cargo test` red on all three CI runners (rusty_av2d overflow).

integration.form: crate (standalone rusty_mp3 0.8.0, rusty_aac 0.5.0, rusty_vorbis 0.1.1; engine library remade-ffmpeg 0.2.0; rff-cli binaries)
integration.dependencies: none for the three codec crates (empty [dependencies]); examples, benches and the CLI use the in-house rusty_alloc global allocator
integration.min_toolchain: Rust 1.85 (crate rust-version); workspace pins 1.95.0 in rust-toolchain.toml; rusty_aac's opt-in AVX-512 tier needs Rust 1.89+
integration.platforms: Windows, macOS and Linux for the CLI; x86-64 gets runtime-detected AVX/AVX2 kernels with scalar fallbacks, and other targets run the scalar paths; rusty_mp3 verified bit-exact on wasm32-wasip1 and wasm32-unknown-unknown
integration.thread_safety: Not documented per type. Decoders and encoders are independent owned values; the encoders spawn `available_parallelism()` scoped threads inside finish/drain; rusty_mp3's stage profiler writes process-global atomics shared by every decoder instance.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: the rff CLI mimics common ffmpeg flags and can install as ffmpeg/ffprobe, but codec and container coverage is a subset, and the Rust library APIs do not replace libavcodec's C API

gotchas: rusty_mp3's per-stage profiler ships in the library on every target except wasm32-unknown-unknown: each stage of each granule calls `Instant::now()` twice and does a global atomic `fetch_add` (about 26 scope pairs per frame, about 1% self-tax per decprof's comment), and those counters are shared across threads.

`decode_pipelined(&[u8]) -> Vec<DecodedAudio>` takes the complete stream and returns all PCM at once (582 MB of f32 for the 27.5-minute benchmark stream), so the 2-core speedup is not available to the streaming `Mp3Decoder` API.

The main README says '100% safe Rust on the core path', but rusty_mp3's synthesis uses `unsafe` AVX intrinsics (matrixing_avx, window_avx) and rusty_aac's SIMD is `unsafe` behind its default `simd` feature; build rusty_aac with `--no-default-features` for a fully safe scalar build.

Main-README figures lag the crate READMEs: the MP3-encoder gap to LAME is still quoted as 0.72/1.08 ODG at 192/128 kb/s, while rusty_mp3's README re-measured 0.08/0.23 on a different corpus; MP3 VBR output was undecodable by FFmpeg through 0.4.1, so pin 0.5.0 or later.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over Symphonia when you also need encoders (AAC-LC, MP3, Vorbis) or FFmpeg-bit-exact MP3 output. Symphonia is the broader decode-only library, and its comparison against libavcodec runs in-process, which is stronger evidence than this repo's CLI timing. Pick glint instead for a C/C++ AAC encoder with a streaming per-frame C ABI. Pick rusty-opus (same organisation, separate repo) for Opus.
verified_claims_summary: First-party, unnamed machine, Rust 1.95.0 thin-LTO builds. rusty_mp3's decode loop (the decprof example) against the FFmpeg CLI's native mp3float decoder (`-f null -`, FFmpeg version not stated) on one 27.5-minute stream, 15 alternated wall-clock pairs: 1,952 vs 2,431 ms on 1 physical core and 1,017 vs 1,455 ms on 2 with the two-thread pipeline; the serial build on 2 cores lost, 1,807 vs 1,445 ms. AAC-LC encode via the rff CLI was 3.2-7.9x faster than FFmpeg 8.1.2's native encoder (unpinned subprocesses, best-of-5, all cores against one), and Vorbis encode about 5.2x faster than libvorbis on 24 cores but about 1.45x slower single-threaded.
status_note: Active (394 commits; last code commit 2026-09-16, last commit a 2026-10-04 install-count banner edit), Apache-2.0, pre-1.0 with 2 open issues and 6 open dependency-bump PRs; the codec crates are small and dependency-free enough to vendor, but they were first split out and published only in July-August 2026.
measurement_notes: For the orchestrator: no correctness bug was found behind the numbers, but there is a measurement flaw in the headline per-core MP3 claim. (1) The FFmpeg arm is the whole ffmpeg CLI with `-f null -`. For audio, libavformat/nullenc.c sets the null muxer's default audio codec to pcm_s16le, so FFmpeg also runs a filtergraph that converts mp3float's fltp output to s16 and then a PCM encoder. The authors' own measurement shows the FFmpeg CLI using about 2 cores with -threads 1 (CPU/wall 1.96), so its pipeline stages run on separate threads; on one pinned core those threads time-share it (FFmpeg's CPU/wall on 1 core is 2,125/2,431 = 0.87). The rusty_mp3 arm is the decprof example: an in-process loop over a file already in memory, keeping all PCM in a Vec. (2) The same table bounds the decoders themselves. With two cores, FFmpeg's whole pipeline takes 1,455 ms, so its single-threaded decoder thread spends at most 1,455 ms decoding, while the serial rusty_mp3 build needs 1,807 ms wall (1,875 ms CPU on one core). Decoder for decoder, libavcodec's mp3float therefore looks at least about 1.25x faster per core (derived from page data; an inference, not a measurement). That matches the authors' earlier CLI-to-CLI '1.20x behind'. So the 1-core '1.24x faster' measures FFmpeg CLI overhead squeezed onto one core, and the 2-core 1.39x is a two-thread pipeline against a single-threaded decoder. The MP3 decode claim should not be treated as a per-core codec win. (3) Neither the MP3 decode table's command nor its affinity masks, CPU model or FFmpeg version is published; commit 55ef2d5 carries only the numbers. codec-bench.ps1 pins to a single logical CPU (`1 -shl $Core`), its frame-count probe and Mpx column are video-shaped, and pinab.py compares two of the project's own binaries by their self-reported 'total ms'. The MP3 table is therefore not reproducible from the committed harnesses. The crate README's control row says '1.30x slower', but 1,807/1,445 = 1.25x. (4) AAC speed (aac_vs_ffmpeg.py) times unpinned CLI subprocesses (best-of-5, wall clock, including process launch, WAV read and MP4 mux), with rusty_aac on all cores against FFmpeg's single-threaded encoder. FFmpeg alone spans 39x-93x realtime on clips of the same length. The script's speed loop reads corp_long_mus_* clips while the README table says 24 s clips. For quality, `decode_neutral` downmixes every decode to mono (`-ac 1`) before PEAQ, so the 'stereo' rows cannot see stereo-image errors. (5) Vorbis matched-rate pair: rff -q:a 8 at 139 kb/s against libvorbis -q:a 5 at 147 kb/s, best-of-7/5 wall clock on an unnamed '24-core box'. The docs name an i7-14650HX only for the VP9 and threading pages. (6) Other findings: the AAC decoder's `dsp::imdct` is still the naive O(N^2) f64 cosine sum flagged in open issue #16 (no maintainer reply). The README install banner rose from 175,858 to 306,805 in a 2026-10-04 docs-only commit. crates.io: rusty_mp3 42,303 downloads, rusty_aac 7,831, rusty_vorbis 1,673, rff-cli 33, remade-ffmpeg 75. New leads, not catalogued: github.com/Remade-With-Rust/rusty_gif (claims GIF encode 1.5-2.5x faster than FFmpeg) and github.com/Remade-With-Rust/rusty_jpeg (claims encode 1.19x and decode 1.05x faster than FFmpeg), both image-codecs and both Rust; rusty_png is already in the catalog.
